The task is to define the primary symbolic meaning of "Heart of the earth" in Christian teaching and biblical interpretation, based on independent knowledge.
In Christian teaching, "heart of the earth" most commonly stands for the tomb or grave where Jesus lay after his death, serving as the place of his burial and the starting point of his resurrection. This draws directly from Matthew 12:40, which parallels the three days Jonah spent in the fish's belly with the 72 hours Jesus would spend in the heart of the earth, pointing to the period between crucifixion and rising again.
